outcome: Incidence of hypotension during caesarean section under spinal anaesthesia
Maximum decrease in mean arterial pressure (MAP) from baseline
cohort: The study included 152 ASA Class II parturients who were scheduled for elective caesarean sections under spinal anaesthesia.
finding: Larger abdominal circumference was significantly associated with a higher incidence of hypotension, more frequent hypotensive episodes, and a greater maximum decrease in mean arterial pressure (MAP) from baseline during caesarean sections under spinal anaesthesia.
mod_finding: Larger abdominal circumference predicts a higher incidence of hypotension during caesarean sections performed under spinal anaesthesia.
cross-section timing: During caesarean section under spinal anaesthesia
